intro: Professionals and everyday users convert pound-feet (lb·ft) to newton-meters (N·m) when working across imperial and si standards in automotive lug nut torque wrench settings, engine dynamometer curves, and industrial fastener specifications. One pound-foot (ft·lbf) equals 1.355818 newton-meters, while 1 newton-meter equals 0.737562 pound-feet. Whether you are verifying torque specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Exact NIST Factor vs. Early Rounding Drift
items: The exact conversion factor from Pound-foot (ft·lbf) to Newton-meter is 1.35581795, derived from the 1959 International Yard and Pound Agreement (1 inch = 25.4 mm, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg).

In structural engineering, CNC machining, or bulk inventory totals, rounding the multiplier to 2 decimal places too early can introduce cumulative tolerance errors; always compute with the full factor and round only the final displayed figure.

faqs.question: How many newton-meters (N·m) are in 1 pound-foot (ft·lbf) (lb·ft)?
faqs.answer: There are 1.35581795 newton-meters (N·m) in 1 pound-foot (ft·lbf) (lb·ft), which rounds to 1.3558 N·m for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 newton-meter equals 0.737562 pound-feet.

faqs.question: How do I convert pound-feet to newton-meters (lb·ft to N·m)?
faqs.answer: To convert pound-feet to newton-meters, use the formula: N·m = lb·ft × 1.35581795. For example, converting 50 lb·ft gives 67.7909 N·m.

faqs.question: What is 50 pound-feet in newton-meters?
faqs.answer: 50 pound-feet (lb·ft) equals exactly 67.7909 newton-meters (N·m) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
